# Build a word search from a list that actually fits

Canonical page: https://nepocore.com/blog/word-search-custom-list-answer-key/

By Nepocore. Published 2026-10-28; updated 2026-11-04.

Choose a grid, useful vocabulary and an answer key, while handling words the generator cannot place.

## Quick answer

Use a focused list of English A–Z words, choose a grid that can fit them, and review the normalized word bank and answer key. Check which words were placed before printing; recognition alone does not test independent spelling.

## Give the puzzle a learning purpose

A word search can reinforce recognition of a focused vocabulary set. Start with a theme such as animals, classroom objects or terms from one lesson. Eight related words with a short follow-up activity can be more useful than thirty unrelated words chosen only to fill a page.

The generator uses English A–Z words. Remove spaces, punctuation and accents deliberately, and tell learners how multiword terms are represented. Avoid placing two answers that differ only by punctuation the generator removes. Review the normalized list so the printed word bank matches the actual hidden entries.

## Match the grid to the longest word

A word cannot fit in a straight line if it is longer than the chosen grid dimension. A 12-letter term needs at least 12 cells in its direction. Even when each word fits individually, a crowded group may not fit together. Word length, shared letters and allowed directions all affect placement.

Begin with a 12 × 12 grid for a short list of moderate-length words, then adjust. Forward horizontal and vertical directions are easier to explain than backward diagonals. Add directions only when they suit the intended learners. The seeded layout lets you regenerate the same set rather than relying on an unrepeatable random page.

1. Enter one theme-based word per line.
2. Choose the grid size and allowed directions.
3. Generate the puzzle and read any unplaced-word notice.
4. Increase the grid or shorten the list when needed.
5. Review the answer key before printing both pages.

## Check the puzzle and the answer key together

Do not silently remove a word that failed to place while leaving it in a learner’s task. Nepocore reports missing entries. Revise the set until the printed bank and grid match what you intend. The answer key is a practical verification tool, not just a teacher convenience.

Read each answer letter by letter in its marked position. Check that a backward word is allowed if one appears. Random filler may accidentally form other words; inspect the grid if that matters for the audience. A generated puzzle still benefits from a quick editorial review.

## Make the printed activity readable

Download the combined PDF for the puzzle and key, or export separate images. Match A4 or Letter settings to the paper and inspect print preview. The puzzle should have enough space for marking without hiding neighboring letters. Avoid printing a small screenshot of a full page.

Keep the answer key separate during the activity. Add a second task, such as defining three terms or using them in sentences, when the goal goes beyond recognition. The tool generates a layout; it does not assess reading level, vocabulary mastery or accessibility needs. Offer a large-print or simpler-direction version when a learner needs it.
